source.title: When Bigger is Worse: A Practitioner's Guide to Model Selection Under Data Scarcity

record.file_problem: The paper is present through its appendices. Some figure text is garbled in extraction, and Appendix B includes a placeholder description rather than complete implementation details; neither makes the document unusable.
record.tranche_reason: The authors use Kaplan/Hoffmann-style scaling and compute-optimal ideas to motivate and interpret a supervised vision experiment, but do not test held-out language-model cross-entropy power laws, their extrapolation, or the parameter/token allocation law. Their results concern detection mAP and efficiency, not the claimed loss measure.
record.gate_note: The paper trains YOLO11 object detectors on rooftop-PV images and reports detection mAP, model-size efficiency, and inference throughput. These are related to the scaling topic but are not held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fitted loss power laws; accordingly, the reported experimental outcomes are recorded with versions ["none"]. The text also cites results from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes COCO-initialised YOLO11 detectors (2.6M–57M parameters) on 897–8,977 rooftop-PV images. It reports detection mAP50, mAP50 per MB and FPS. It measures no held-out cross-entropy loss, fits no power law in parameters, data or compute, and extrapolates no fit. It invokes Chinchilla's 20:1 token ratio only as an interpretive analogy, treating 16×16 patches as tokens, and does not test it. Its target is a generic 'bigger is better' prior rather than any listed version. The mAP-vs-size results in supervised fine-tuning are a related but different construct, so they belong under fits_no_version. T4 is a poor fit: the paper does not use the finding as a tool for its own method. It discusses and analogises the scaling laws, hence 'discusses'/T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the scaling prior is 'conditional': it holds when data are abundant and pretraining transfers, and inverts in data-scarce Earth-observation detection. There the smallest YOLO11 matches the best accuracy at 22× higher efficiency. They also conclude that resolution, not data volume, is the dominant allocation lever because it drives Pareto dominance. They claim their results 'confirm' a Chinchilla-ratio prediction, but this rests on a patch-as-token analogy, not a test.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised fine-tuning of COCO-initialized YOLO11 object detectors on annotated images; detection mAP, storage efficiency, and throughput are measured rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy. The paper analogizes 16 × 16 image patches to tokens when discussing a compute-optimal ratio, but does not test that ratio as a loss-allocation rule.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported detection outcomes vary across model size, dataset fraction, and input resolution. The study does not test sensitivity to loss-fitting choices or fitting methods.

fits_no_version.finding: In COCO-initialised YOLO11 fine-tuning on about 9k drone images, the smallest model has the highest mAP50 per MB (0.841 vs 0.038 for X). Its absolute mAP50 is near the top (0.459 vs 0.464 for S per text). L and X are lowest in mean mAP50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In data-scarce supervised detection fine-tuning, increasing detector size within one family does not improve detection accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Data gains are front-loaded and saturate faster for the smallest model: N gains +0.007 from 50% to 100% data, L gains +0.025. mAP50 falls with params per training sample (an unfitted negative log-linear trend).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small-data detection fine-tuning, larger models remain data-limited and the data-to-parameter ratio predicts accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher input resolution raises mAP50 for most variants (N: 0.409 to 0.444). Resolution and data contribute comparable relative efficiency gains (+8% vs +10%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input resolution is a scaling axis for small-object detection comparable to data volume.

fits_no_version.finding: COCO-pretrained zero-shot mAP50 is ≤0.0022 for all variants, decreasing from N to L.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: COCO pretraining gives no zero-shot transfer to rooftop-PV detection, regardless of size.

record.problems: The evidence is confined to one detector family, one geographic context, and one object-detection task. Reported primary results generally lack numerical error bars or confidence intervals despite three seeds; the authors refer to run-to-run variance without quantifying it in the presented text. Some appendix implementation details are left as a placeholder, and figure text is partly garbled in the supplied extraction.
record.rows_left_out: No other text-stated numeric outcomes on the study's own detection experiments were extracted beyond the principal efficiency, matched-configuration, resolution, zero-shot, learning-curve, and aggregate-trend results listed. Results cited from other papers are excluded.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured; no power law is fitted in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit is extrapolated to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep; the Chinchilla 20:1 ratio is invoked only by analogy (patches as tokens) and not measured.
The variants differ jointly in depth and width with parameter count; no fixed-parameter shape comparison is made.
The study is in vision detection fine-tuning but measures mAP, not loss, and fits no power-law form. Its 'negative log-linear' mAP vs params/sample trend is unfitted and not a loss scaling law.
No relation between language-model scale or pretraining loss and downstream task performance is measured.
No fitting choices, exponents or curve bending are analysed.

record.verdict_notes: Supervised object-detection fine-tuning study; outcomes are mAP/efficiency/FPS, so all rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The paper has internal numeric inconsistencies: Table 5 vs main text on best mAP50, and the D.2 text (0.548; 416 px only) vs Table 7. Its uses of Kaplan and Hoffmann are rhetorical framing and an analogy, not tests. Changed relation/tranche from uses_without_test/T4 to discusses/T6 because the finding is not used as a tool for a method.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured, and no power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute is fitted.
No small-run loss fit is extrapolated to larger runs.

No fixed-compute language-model allocation experiment or loss-minimising parameter/token split is measured. The paper invokes a token-to-parameter rule by approximating image patches as tokens, but does not test that rule.
The evaluated YOLO11 variants share an architecture; the study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study examines supervised vision detection, but does not measure cross-entropy loss or test whether a power-law form holds in that regime.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss is measured.
No fitted language-model exponents, fitting-method comparisons, or bends in language-model loss curves are analyzed.
